Meet your professor

Kenechukwu
“Ken” Ezekwem, PhD

Clinical Assistant ProfessorManagement & Analytics · NYU SPS

Better analysis starts with a better question.

Professor Ken teaches at the intersection of analytics, AI, and business operations. His courses connect quantitative reasoning with practical decisions, inspectable evidence, and responsible use of technology.

He emphasizes hands-on learning: define the problem, examine the data, choose a defensible method, check the result, and explain what it supports. A chart or a statistical output is a starting point for judgment.

He is also Faculty Advisor to the Management & Analytics Professionals Society (MAPS). This Learning Studio extends his classroom with small experiments, worked explanations, and resources students can revisit.

How we learn here

Start with a decision

Name the stakeholder and the choice before selecting a statistical procedure.

Make the reasoning visible

Show counts, denominators, units, assumptions, and limits so the work can be inspected.

Learn through experiments

Predict the result, change an input, compare the evidence, and explain the difference.

Keep extending

Use the optional toolkit during or after the course. Build confidence at your own pace.
